new_statements.quote: [p.782] Word-stress does not seem to have existed in PNNH as it appears to have been innovated along different rules in Sakao, Lehali, and Shark Bay. [...] [p.794] Stage 1. Word-stress was innovated, usually on the penultimate vowel. e.g.: miite 'snake' < 'nwata < PNNH nwata; tahe 'shark' < pa'geo < PNNH pageo; but: tata 'breadfruit' < 'paego < PNNH paego. [...] [p.795] Stage 6. [...] Posttonic vowels following free tonic vowels are lost, whereas posttonic vowels following blocked tonic vowels go to schwa (phonemically interpreted as /e/) while the tonic vowel is lengthened. new_statements.rule_in_words: Diachronic account from the author's own Shark Bay wordlist: stress arose on the penultimate vowel of the pre-Shark Bay form (a few words antepenultimate); subsequent loss of post-tonic vowels after open stressed vowels and reduction of post-tonic vowels to /e/ (schwa) after closed stressed vowels, with lengthening of the stressed vowel, left stress non-contrastive ('no longer emic') in the modern language. The synchronic position is not stated; from the derivations it falls on the long vowel before final /e/ (mii.te 'snake', nee.ze 'fish', pee.te 'taro') and otherwise on what is now the final syllable (ta'he 'shark', monosyllables mi 'sun', gar 'stone') -- i.e. predictable, but this locus is an inference, not Guy's wording.
new_statements.exceptions: Stage 1: 'usually' penultimate; tata 'breadfruit' < 'paego given as an antepenultimate case. p.796 Remark: 'Too little is known about the Shark Bay language to allow a complete understanding of its diachronic phonology'.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level, isolated lexical items (wordlist data, c. Tryon 1976 list 66 collected by Guy); statement is diachronic plus a synchronic claim that stress is non-phonemic; no phrase-level information.
new_statements.identity_note: Guy's 'Shark Bay' data are his own wordlist published as Tryon (1976) list 66 'Shark Bay I' (collector J. Guy), which Tryon (2010: fn.17) equates with Ngen (shar1244); Tryon's list 67 'Shark Bay II' and Lorediakarkar (lore1244, 'Nethalp') are the neighbouring varieties and are not the object of Guy's section.

sources.note: p.782: word-stress did not exist in PNNH and 'appears to have been innovated along different rules in Sakao, Lehali, and Shark Bay'. Section 'Shark Bay diachronic phonology' pp.793-796: phoneme inventory (7 vowels), then p.794 'Stage 1. Word-stress was innovated, usually on the penultimate vowel' (exception t a t a 'breadfruit' < 'paego, antepenult); p.795 Stage 6: posttonic vowels after free tonic vowels lost, after blocked tonic vowels reduced to schwa (/e/) with the tonic vowel lengthened; 'Stress is then no longer emic.' No explicit synchronic statement of where stress now falls.
